analytical_models.equation_role: Estimate stacking fault energy from thermodynamic free energy of the γ→ε transformation
analytical_models.model_note: Same calculation gives 40 mJ/m2 at -77 °C and 32 mJ/m2 at -196 °C; Table 1 supplies the ΔG_i^(γ→ε) terms.

analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the work hardening exponent n and strength coefficient K; work hardening divided into two stages n1 (low strain) and n2 (high strain)
analytical_models.model_name: Hollomon formula σ = K·ε^n (lnσ = lnK + n·lnε)
analytical_models.model_note: RT work hardening exponents are the lowest of the three temperatures.

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimate the alloy density from composition
analytical_models.model_name: Kim et al. density equation ργ = 8.10 − 0.101(Al%) − 0.41(C%) − 0.0085(Mn%)
analytical_models.model_note: Estimated density 7.078 g/cm3; measured density 7.114 g/cm3.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Experimental steel melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
Ingot reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
Forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm followed by cooling to RT in the furnace; starting forging temperature 1100 °C and finishing 950 °C.

Tensile deformed to fracture at RT at a strain rate of 0.001 s-1 (10-3 s-1); parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1.5 mm; three samples tested per condition and averaged; an extensometer was used.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Quasi-static tensile test to fracture; extensometer used; average of three specimens per condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1.5 mm

elongation.value: total elongation ≈33% at RT (engineering stress-strain curve terminates near strain 33)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering and true stress-strain (with work hardening rate) curves at RT shown in Fig. 2a,b (25 °C, grey curve)

structures.overall_structure: Tensile-deformed (RT) fully austenitic microstructure of the uniformly deformed section. Crystal orientations of the deformed austenite grains concentrate in {111} and {001}. No mechanical twins form at RT; deformation proceeds by planar glide with microbands along {111} planes. LAGB fraction 56.0% and HAGB fraction 44.0%.

unmapped_findings: Stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel at RT is estimated to be 61 mJ/m2; it decreases with decreasing temperature to 40 mJ/m2 at -77 °C and 32 mJ/m2 at -196 °C (eqs. 2-4, Table 1).
Crystal orientations of the RT tensile-deformed austenite grains concentrate in {111} and {001} as a result of coordinated plastic deformation (Fig. 3c).
RT tensile sample shows no mechanical twins (mechanical twins appear only in the sample deformed at -196 °C), consistent with its high SFE.
The work hardening rate of the RT tensile sample decreases continuously with strain, whereas the -77 °C and -196 °C samples show a near-linear work hardening rate with strain.
Grain-boundary fractions of the RT tensile-deformed sample: low-angle grain boundaries (2-15°) 56.0% and high-angle grain boundaries (>15°) 44.0% (Fig. 3f).
Geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) accumulate at low-angle grain boundaries, indicating more severe local deformation in these regions (Fig. 3g-i).
Measured density of the experimental steel is 7.114 g/cm3 and the estimated density (Kim et al. equation) is 7.078 g/cm3.
